newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian metalworkers call two-hour strike Friday.
newsitem.headline: Italian metalworkers call two-hour strike Friday.

text.p: Italian metalworkers unions said on Thursday they would stage a two-hour strike on Friday, their third stoppage in a bitter dispute over contracts.

Union leaders told reporters the strike was in response to proposals, which they considered unacceptable, presented to Italian Labour Minister Tiziano Treu by the metalworkers employers' federation, Federmeccanica.

They planned to present their own proposal to Treu on Friday. Federmeccanica head Michele Figurati told reporters earlier that he presented his list of demands to Treu, but Treu "didn't seem very impressed."
Figurati said the chances of reaching a swift deal to end the months-long labour dispute were slender because the union's position was equally firm.
Treu, who has been locked in talks with employers and unions all day, had said he hoped to be able to submit a proposal to metalworkers by Saturday. He gave no further details.

Unions representing 1.7 million workers in the metalworking and engineering sector, which accounts for about 40 percent of total manufacturing output in Italy, are locked in dispute with management over pay increases for 1996-1998.

Union leaders said earlier that Federmeccanica was talking tough. Figurati said his group's position was essentially that it wanted a commitment from the government to lower labour costs, with special additional measures for the poor south.
Metalworkers' contracts expired in June and unions have recently held two national strikes in support of their claims for wage rises.
